differences.what: Four storeys of stone, round-arched shop fronts under three rows of round-arched windows with hoods and a bracketed cornice, the Madison Street front to the left and the Dearborn Street front to the right, where the engraving shows them
The cut-off corner with its arched entrance, the raised crest over it, and the pediment over the Madison Street front's east end
The corner's crest is a pedimented aedicule in the engraving; it is drawn as a little hipped attic with a round window
The windows near the corner, the 'CHICAGO TRIBUNE' sign and the round ornaments over the entrance are not drawn; the corner's piers are plain
The stone reads as the 1904 kit's Lemont limestone, warmer than the engraving's paper

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
